title: A Job Interview
description: Four recordings about job interviews: an interview, a voicemail, a chat between friends and a talk with advice.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · The interview
parts.intro: You will hear Mrs Clark interviewing Ben for a weekend job in a bookshop.

script.speaker: Mrs Clark
script.text: Good morning, Ben. Please sit down. Thanks for coming to the interview for the weekend assistant job at our bookshop.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Thank you for seeing me, Mrs Clark. I'm really pleased to be here.

script.speaker: Mrs Clark
script.text: I see you're still at school. Will you be able to work every Saturday and Sunday?

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Saturdays, yes, definitely. On Sundays I play football in the morning, but I could start after lunch, if that's all right.

script.speaker: Mrs Clark
script.text: That would be fine. Now, have you ever worked in a shop before?

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Not in a shop, no. But last summer I helped at my uncle's fruit stall for six weeks, so I'm used to talking to customers and handling money.

script.speaker: Mrs Clark
script.text: Good. And why do you want to work with us in particular?

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Well, I read a lot, mostly adventure stories, and I come here nearly every week. I think I could recommend books to people because I know the shelves quite well.

script.speaker: Mrs Clark
script.text: That's useful. The pay is seven pounds fifty an hour, and you'd start with a training day on the first Saturday of the month.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: That sounds great. Is there anything I should bring?

script.speaker: Mrs Clark
script.text: Just a form of identification. We'll let you know by Friday.

parts.title: Part 2 · A voicemail
parts.intro: You will hear a voicemail message from Jack, who works for a recruitment agency.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Hello, Mai. This is Jack from Bright Futures Recruitment. I'm calling about the office assistant interview you have next week.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Unfortunately, the company has had to change the day. It was on Tuesday, but now it will be on Wednesday, the ninth of July, at quarter past ten.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: The address hasn't changed. It's the Green Tower on Park Road, on the fourth floor. Please go to reception and ask for Mr Hughes. If you come by car, don't park in front of the building, because it costs a lot. There's a cheaper car park behind the station.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: The interview will take about forty minutes, and there'll be a short writing test, so please bring a pen. You don't need to bring your certificates because we already have copies.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Could you phone me back before Monday afternoon to confirm that Wednesday suits you? If I don't hear from you, I'll try again. My number is on the email I sent last week. Good luck!

parts.title: Part 3 · After the interview
parts.intro: You will hear Peter talking to his friend Linh after her interview.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: So how did it go, Linh? You've been very quiet since you came out.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: I'm not sure, to be honest. The first part was fine, but then they asked me about a time when I solved a problem at work, and my mind went completely blank.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Oh no. What did you say?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: I talked about the day the printer broke, which isn't very impressive. Afterwards I remembered a much better story about a customer who lost his bag.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Well, don't worry. Everyone forgets things when they're nervous. Did they seem friendly?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Very. The manager laughed at my joke, so that was a good sign. But another person kept writing notes and never smiled, which made me nervous.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: That doesn't mean anything. Some people just concentrate hard.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Maybe. I also forgot to ask about holidays and salary. I'd planned to, but the interview finished so quickly.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: You could send them an email tonight and thank them for their time. You can ask your questions then.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: That's a great idea. I'll do it as soon as I get home.

parts.title: Part 4 · Interview advice
parts.intro: You will hear a careers adviser giving a talk to students.

script.speaker: Ms Hall
script.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I've been a careers adviser for fifteen years, and today I'd like to share four simple ideas that can make a real difference in a job interview.

script.speaker: Ms Hall
script.text: Firstly, research the company. It sounds obvious, but a surprising number of candidates arrive knowing almost nothing. If you can mention something the company has done recently, the interviewer will see that you're serious.

script.speaker: Ms Hall
script.text: Secondly, practise your answers aloud. Reading them in your head isn't the same. Ask a friend to pretend to be the interviewer, and you'll feel much calmer on the day.

script.speaker: Ms Hall
script.text: Thirdly, think carefully about what you wear. You don't have to buy expensive clothes, but you should look tidy. Choose something comfortable, because feeling uncomfortable will make you more nervous.

script.speaker: Ms Hall
script.text: Finally, arrive early, but not too early. Ten minutes before the interview is perfect. If you arrive an hour before, the staff might feel under pressure. And remember, if you don't get the job, it isn't a failure. Every interview teaches you something.
